solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Correctly predict charge covering sources of metal

indicators.note: covering says the first piece wraps around the second, which sits inside it

parts.note: a charge is a fee
ores are the rocks metals are extracted from

explanation.surface: Someone guesses rightly that a levy will be placed on raw materials for metalworking.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to see an event coming before it happens, so it is a synonym for predicting correctly.

clue.text: Cash fee cut — I'm prepared to confront consequences

indicators.note: prepared signals the letters are worked into a new arrangement, as food is prepared

explanation.surface: Someone whose payment is being slashed accepts they must deal with what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means accepting the unpleasant results of one's actions, that is confronting them.

clue.text: Embarrassed anger over court — advise new course

indicators.note: in a down clue over says the earlier pieces sit above the next one

parts.note: embarrassed people go red
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Someone red-faced and furious at a legal hearing tells another to take a different route.
explanation.definitionFit: To redirect is to send something or someone along a different path, so to advise a new course.

clue.text: Time to escape from standard footwear

indicators.note: to escape from says that letter leaves the word for standard

parts.note: stock means standard, as in a stock reply

explanation.surface: A moment to break free of standard-issue shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sock is a garment worn on the foot, so a piece of footwear.

clue.text: Cake, high calorie, nothing left

indicators.note: high, as in drunk or intoxicated, signals the letters are jumbled
left says that the letter for nothing has departed from the word calorie

parts.note: O is the round symbol for zero, or nothing

explanation.surface: A cake that is rich in calories, with none remaining on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from CALORIE and the remaining CALRIE, rearranged under 'high', gives the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry cake filled with cream and iced with chocolate.

clue.text: Ivan turning up at entrance to plan route

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the name Ivan is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Ivan appears at the gate to work out which way to go.
explanation.definitionFit: To navigate is to plan and follow a course from one place to another.

clue.text: Attempt nocturnal types mounted

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means the word climbs, so it is read upwards

parts.note: bats are creatures active at night

explanation.surface: An effort by night creatures to climb up something.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is an idiom for making an attempt.

clue.text: Shambolic tea on terrace is caricatured initially

parts.note: cha is a colloquial word for tea

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the last four words

explanation.surface: A messy tea party on a terrace is mocked in a cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambolic is a British informal word for disorganised, which is a synonym for chaotic.

clue.text: Obvious call — car's tyre needs changing

indicators.note: needs changing says the letters must be put into a different order

explanation.surface: An easy decision: the car's tyre needs replacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crystal clear is perfectly transparent, so plainly obvious.

clue.text: Feature of will — something fishy, not quite licit, on reflection?

parts.note: a cod is a fish, so something fishy in a literal sense

indicators.note: on reflection says the shortened word is read backwards, as in a mirror
not quite says the word licit loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A legal document is called suspicious and barely lawful by a doubting heir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something fishy' reads as suspicion but is literal: a fish. 'not quite' drops the T of licit, and 'on reflection' turns the remaining letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is an addition or amendment attached to a will, so it is one of its features.

clue.text: At heart Jamie, seaman, extremely lively in friendly way

indicators.note: at heart means take the inner letters of the name Jamie

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a standard abbreviation for a sailor

indicators.note: extremely asks for only the two end letters of the word lively

explanation.surface: Jamie, a sailor, is described as very lively and good-natured at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiable means good-natured, so the adverb describes acting in a friendly manner.

clue.text: Wings of the raven? Another bird

indicators.note: wings are the outer edges, so take the end letters of the words the and raven

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher asks about the raven's wings and then names a second species.
explanation.definitionFit: The tern is a slender seabird, a different species from the raven, hence another bird.

clue.text: Long-lasting series of Superman, enthralling

indicators.note: series of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A long-running run of Superman stories proves gripping.
explanation.definitionFit: Permanent means enduring indefinitely, a direct synonym for long-lasting.

clue.text: At first popular — very, our new food supplier

indicators.note: at first means take the opening letter of popular
new signals the letters of the two words are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A caterer is initially very popular, says a review of a new venture.
explanation.definitionFit: A purveyor is a supplier of goods, especially provisions such as food.

clue.text: He won't forget Jumbo?

definitions.meaning: the proverb says this animal never forgets
Jumbo was a famous circus animal of the African kind, and its name became a nickname for the species

explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'an elephant never forgets' and the famous Jumbo both point to the same large animal.

clue.text: Procession Democrat organised about first of October

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters surround the next piece
organised says the letters of Democrat are arranged into a new order
first of picks out the opening letter of October

explanation.surface: A US Democratic politician arranges a parade for early October.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' shuffles DEMOCRAT into MOTRCADE, and 'about' puts it around O from 'first of October'.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcade is a procession of cars, typically escorting a dignitary.

clue.text: Part of veteran thematic song?

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An old soldier's music on a recurring theme is perhaps a song.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a rousing or solemn song, such as a national one.

clue.text: Long and impressive European film

parts.note: pic is informal for a picture, that is a film

explanation.surface: A grand, lengthy movie made in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic as an adjective describes something heroic in scale, lengthy and grand.

clue.text: Prominent street captivates outsider

indicators.note: captivates means holds captive, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner or outsider

explanation.surface: A well-known road charms a newcomer from elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means most noticeable or projecting, a synonym of prominent.

clue.text: Shipping company policy

definitions.meaning: a shipping firm operating a fleet is called a ..., such as Cunard
a party ... is its official policy

explanation.definitionFit: Line names both a fleet-owning shipping firm and an official stance or policy.

clue.text: Drops artist home

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist
in means at home

explanation.surface: A painter goes indoors and drops off.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain is water falling in drops; the clue uses the plural noun to describe the precipitation.

clue.text: Payment per animal he linked to commercial era

parts.note: an ad is a commercial advertisement
an age is an era

explanation.surface: A man associated with the age of advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Headage is a subsidy paid to farmers according to the number of livestock held.

clue.text: Serve as comfort to prisoner, unaccompanied

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
sole means alone, without company

explanation.surface: Offer solace to an inmate kept in solitary.
explanation.definitionFit: To console someone is to comfort them in grief or disappointment.

clue.text: Rugby team assemble about noon

indicators.note: about means the gathering word goes round the next piece

parts.note: to muster is to gather or assemble

explanation.surface: A rugby squad gathers at around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Munster is a province of Ireland whose professional rugby union team carries its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Munster Rugby is a well-known Irish professional club, so it is an example of a rugby team.
